Breakwater Studios and the Obamas' Higher Ground will stream The Eyes of Ghana on YouTube Nov. 17 in a novel partnership with social media star IShowSpeed , aka Darren Watkins, who is also a producer on the film.

The documentary, directed by Ben Proudfoot and executive produced by President Barack Obama and Michelle Obama, will show on IShowSpeed's YouTube Channel, which has more than 62 million subscribers worldwide.

The awards contender officially shortlisted for Best Feature Documentary and Best Score at the 42nd IDA Documentary Awards, follows a Ghanaian cameraman's extraordinary mission to rescue a hidden film archive documenting the birth of African independence. The 90-minute film follows veteran Ghanaian cinematographer Chris Hesse, who served as personal cameraman to Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's first president and a leading voice for African liberation. As his eyesight fades, Hesse races against time to rescue more than 1,000 films capturing the continent's struggle for independence in the 1950s and 60s. Hidden for decades after Nkrumah's overthrow in a 1966 coup, the archive becomes a bridge between generations to fill in their lost history. Five years ago, after a chance encounter, Hesse asked fellow documentarian Proudfoot to tell his story.

During his Speed Does Africa tour earlier this year, the creator visited Accra, told viewers he was "back home" and shared that his ancestry traces to Ghana.

"Over six decades ago Chris Hesse picked up a camera and documented one of the most pivotal moments in world history," says Ethan Lewis, Head of Non-Fiction at Higher Ground. "Now, thanks to iShowSpeed and this historic, precedent setting partnership, this history will be shared for all to see for free."

The Eyes of Ghana opened the TIFF Docs program in 2025

at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival and had its international premiere in competition at the BFI London Film Festival. Its honors include the Special Jury Prize and Best Documentary at the Africa International Film Festival in Lagos, Audience Awards at the Hamptons International and Annapolis Film Festivals, and Heartland Film Festival's Jimmy Stewart Legacy Award.

Cinematographer Brandon Somerhalder ( Come See Me in the Good Light ) shot The Eyes of Ghana across multiple formats, including sequences captured on Imax 65mm film.

The film is produced by Proudfoot, Nana Adwoa Frimpong, Moses Bwayo, Anita Afonu, Brandon Somerhalder, Ethan Lewis and Vinnie Malhotra. In addition to President Barack Obama and Michelle Obama, executive producers include Sir John Akomfrah, Kofi Amoo-Gottfried, Paula Madison, Dan and Lian Gill, Max Johnson, Jonathan E. Lim, Michael Risley, Josh Rosenberg, David Treatman and Esther Wojcicki.

Original score from Academy Awardwinner Kris Bowers, Proudfoot's frequent collaborator.

IShowSpeed, born Darren Watkins Jr., is an American creator and entertainer whose work connects audiences across borders and cultures. A Cincinnati native with more than 200 million followers, he was named to the inaugural TIME100 Creators list and ranked No. 1 on Rolling Stone's 2025 Most Influential Creators list. His honors also include consecutive Streamer of the Year awards in 2024 and 2025.

articles.title: Howie Mandel to Host 'Joker's Wild' Game Show Revival
articles.summary: Sony is producing the show, which is set to go into syndication on CBS-owned stations in the fall of 2027.
articles.content:
Sony Pictures Television is putting a new spin on the classic game show The Joker's Wild .

The studio is set to start filming on a new version of the show, with Howie Mandel as host. The Joker's Wild will debut in syndication on CBS-owned stations in fall 2027.

Sony doing business with CBS is notable, as the two companies had a protracted legal fight over two other game shows: Jeopardy! and Wheel of Fortune . The two sides settled a lawsuit a year ago that involved disputes over distribution contracts for the Sony-produced shows. "I love that we're bringing The Joker's Wild back," said Mandel. "It's such a fun, crazy show, and getting to be a part of that is a real honor. There's something great about taking a show people have loved for years and seeing what you can do with it today. I'm excited to get in there, have some laughs, and probably make a little bit of a mess along the way. That's usually when I'm having the most fun."

Jack Barry created and hosted the original version of the show. It had a brief revival in the early 1990s, and Snoop Dogg hosted a new version of The Joker's Wild on TBS and TNT from 2017-19.

Louis Carr , who took over as president of BET Media Group last year after the departure of former president/CEO Scott Mills, is exiting. Carr had previously served as BET's president of media sales but was elevated to president last December while maintaining his media sales role, reporting to George Cheeks, then chair of TV media at Paramount Skydance. He also wrote the book "Dirty Little Secrets" and "Little Black Book: Daily Motivations for Business and Personal Growth." articles.content:
The Beatlemaniac might be the easiest category to shop for. More than 60 years after the Fab Four first took the world by storm, there's no shortage of new music releases, archival box sets, photo books and collectible merchandise to keep even the most devoted fans busy.

This year is particularly fruitful for vinyl collectors, with a new five-LP "Rubber Sou"l box set featuring previously unreleased studio recordings and a fresh stereo mix, alongside a special-edition pressing of Paul McCartney ‘s latest solo album, "The Boys of Dungeon Lane." There's also a new soundtrack accompanying the Wings documentary "Man on the Run," available in collectible colored vinyl editions. Related Stories 'PUBG' Live-Action Series From Donald Glover, Stephen Glover in Development at Netflix ‘Virgin River’ Renewed for Season 9 to Become Netflix’s Longest-Running Original Scripted Series

For fans more interested in the band's history, George Harrison's "The Third Eye: Early Photographs" features more than 200 never-before-seen photographs taken by Harrison. Meanwhile, Erika White's "Meat the Beatles : The Butcher Cover" unpacks the story behind the band's controversial 1966 "Yesterday" and "Today" album artwork, while Lennon devotees get a deluxe "Power to the People" Blu-ray box set featuring restored footage of his 1972 Madison Square Garden concerts.

Ahead, the best Beatles gifts to shop in 2026.

The Beatles' 1965 classic gets a major upgrade with this new five-LP box set, featuring a fresh stereo mix by Giles Martin and Sam Okell, previously unreleased studio recordings and the original mono and U.S. editions. An accompanying 88-page hardcover book offers a deeper look at the making of one of the band's most influential albums.

For Beatles fans who already have an extensive record collection, this special-edition pressing of "Rubber Soul" offers something a little different. The collectible LP features animated zoetrope artwork that comes to life when the record spins under the right lighting.

Paul McCartney returned with his first new solo album in more than five years in 2026, and this two-LP release includes three previously unreleased tracks and an alternate mix of his duet with former bandmate Ringo Starr.

Released alongside the 2026 documentary chronicling Paul McCartney's post-Beatles years with Wings, this soundtrack brings together music from one of the most transformative periods of his career. Collectors can choose from special-edition pressings, including an Amazon-exclusive orange vinyl and a taxi-yellow edition from Third Man Records.

Paul McCartney's post-Beatles career gets the oral-history treatment in this book chronicling the formation, success and eventual dissolution of Wings. The new 2026 paperback edition includes an additional conversation between McCartney and Morgan Neville, director of the documentary "Man on the Run."

For Beatles obsessives who know every lyric and recording session, this book offers a different way into the band's history. Authors Gary Kemp and Simon Halfon explore the extraordinary social and cultural world of manager Brian Epstein during his final year, using his personal address book to trace the people and relationships surrounding the Fab Four.

The Beatles' psychedelic world gets an unexpected collectible treatment with this model train set from British toy manufacturer Hornby. Featuring "Yellow Submarine"-inspired artwork across a miniature Eurostar.

For a more affordable holiday keepsake, these playful Beatles ornaments turn recognizable album artwork and musical imagery into miniature Christmas decorations. Designs include a "Now and Then" mixtape, "Rubber Soul"-inspired artwork and a "Yellow Submarine" drum set, with several options priced under $30.

Beatlemania gets the building-block treatment with this collectible construction set from MEGA. But act fast: the set sold out immediately upon release and is now being resold in limited quanitites on sites like Ebay.

Abbey Road Studios celebrates six decades of "Revolver" with this exclusive heavyweight cotton T-shirt. Featuring Robert Freeman's photography alongside the album's recording dates and track list, the design pays tribute to the groundbreaking 1966 sessions that helped redefine what the Beatles could achieve in the studio.

John Lennon and Yoko Ono's landmark 1972 Madison Square Garden performances get an extensive re-release in this deluxe Blu-ray collection. Featuring restored concert footage, the documentary One to One: John & Yoko and a 128-page book, the set offers a deeper look at Lennon's early solo years.

For the Beatles fan who already owns every record, coffee table book and vintage tee, "Meat the Beatles: The Butcher Cover" digs into one of the band's strangest — and most collectible — pieces of lore. Erika White. The image sparked instant outrage, a Capitol Records recall and decades of collector obsession. The new book traces the story behind the chaotic photo session led by. photographer Robert Whitaker. It doesn't ship out until November but if you pre-order it now you'll thank yourself for thinking ahead once the holidays roll around.

"The Boys of Dungeon Lane," is Beatles legend Paul McCartney's new solo album, and a highly-anticipated release for any Beatlemaniac. This limited-edition vinyl is available exclusively at Amazon and pressed in an exclusive white hue. The set includes a 12-page lyric booklet and embossed cover artwork.

"1964: Eyes of the Storm," by McCartney and historian Jill Lepore, features more than 274 largely unseen images from the legendary months between 1963-1964 when The Beatles became an international sensation — all taken on McCartney's 35mm camera. The hefty tome also includes an candid forward written by McCartney and Lepore's essay "Beatleland." Check out more pop-culture coffee table books here.

Acclaimed music anthologist and writer Philip Norman utilizes years of research and first-hand interviews with those close to the Fab Four in this expansive biography, published 11 years after the iconic rock band split up and, most notably, a year after John Lennon's assassination. The epic tale charts the English stars from their humble beginnings in Liverpool, to their astonishing heights of fame, to their acrimonious split. This edition is updated to include Paul McCartney's 1997 knighting and Lennon's 1980 assassination.

John Lennon has cited Braun's biography as the most honest account of the band's hey-day, even better than Hunter Davies' much more popular, and also very good, biographical "Beatles Book." Braun takes readers through a nothing-is-off-limits ride-along with the band-members, showcasing each musician's famous wit, even when it gets them in trouble at times.

Quality prints are a sophisticated way for music-lovers to decorate the house and showcase their taste without being ostentatious. This black-and-white Huckleberry print shows a rare photo of the four Beatles wading through a pool in 1964. Shot by John Loengard for the Life Picture Collection, it's part of a limited-edition set of 495 prints, numbered and certified with a story of the image on the back of the print.

This LEGO building kit is part puzzle, part game and part art. The set comes with pieces to build a portrait of any four of the Beatles, whose end product measures to be a 15.5″ square, to be displayed on your wall or shelf anywhere in your home.

Spread some Beatles love while on the road with this adorable Yellow Submarine decal sticker. Place it on your rearview window and you might even make friends with the car behind you while stuck in traffic.

Decorate anything from your laptop, water bottle to notebooks with these vibrant, large stickers featuring artistic images and graphics from vintage Beatles posters and magazine features. The pack comes with 24 different stickers, sized 2.5″ x 3.5″.

Any guitar player inspired by Lennon and Harrison's impressive riffs will love this collectible tin, that comes with 15 high-quality guitar picks printed with iconic Beatles imagery.

articles.title: 5 Most Outrageous Missions in Grand Theft Auto History
articles.summary: There's nothing more synonymous with Grand Theft Auto than unmitigated freedom. I'll never forget cuing up the Grand Theft Auto 3 disc on my PS2 in high school, thinking, "Wow, I can literally go anywhere and do anything." It was an incredibly overwhelming but empowering feeling, and one that Rockstar has continued to build upon […]
articles.content:
But like every ecosystem, there is an indisputable spectrum that spans from the wacky and absurd all the way up to the rigid peak of order and structure. Somewhere in between is where “societal norms” reside. Grand Theft Auto always did a great job of satirizing the spectrum, especially the more outrageous side of civilization. Between selling illicit goods, wacking the competition, and brokering deals, players would occasionally be asked to embrace hilarity and chaos or take on the darkest and most depraved tasks. Everything from breaking into a military black site to steal experimental tech to personally handling the torture of an unlucky recipient, Rockstar has repeatedly found ways to have players engage in situations they never would have imagined when first booting up the game. Let's take a look at some of the missions that made us laugh, cringe, or question what in the hell we were actually playing.

Do you remember The Truth? No, I'm not talking about some random undisclosed secret, but the wild hippie conspiracy theorist who moonlights as a marijuana farmer. When a man of such stature beckons you to break into a secret military installation known as Area 69 (subtle, Rockstar) to steal an experimental jetpack, what do you do? Well, of course, you do what he says. I mean, how could you not? As CJ, the main protagonist and player character for GTA: San Andreas , there's no reason you can't single-handedly take on the military defenses in place at such a facility.

Of course, this facility is actually an underground complex. You'll have to tackle targeting defense systems, military personnel, and all sorts of chaos and disaster. Once you find your objective, you'll be leaving with a jetpack on your back. At this point in the story, you've come a long way from neighborhood shootouts with the Ballas gang, a rival to CJ's own Grove Street crew. It feels almost surreal, like the game morphed into some twisted espionage or sci-fi adventure.

Players' first outing in Vice City is set during the 1980s. Tommy Vercetti comes to town and gets mixed up with the local criminal element. But not every paying customer is a completely crooked gangster or underboss. In fact, Tommy finds himself on the payroll for the popular (and fictitious) rock band, Love Fist. Tommy is often at their beck and call. At one point, he delivers a potent concoction of cocaine and “boomshine” known as “Love Juice” to the band. After all, if they're going to be rock stars, they have to party like rock stars. But at one point, Jezz, Willy, Dick, and Percy (see a pattern there?) attract the attention of a homicidal stalker who is hell-bent on eliminating the band. At one point, the shifty bugger dresses as a female groupie in an attempt to assassinate the band. Tommy runs him down and seemingly kills him in a thrilling chase sequence.

However, the man's vengeance is not over. He survived, and during a mission where Tommy escorts the band in a limousine, it is revealed that he's outfitted the limo with an explosive that will detonate should the speed of the vehicle drop below a particular threshold. Where's Keanu when you need him, right? Players have to keep the limo speeding through town and avoiding collisions while the band defuses the potentially explosive surprise.

Grand Theft Auto 4 famously received a fun story expansion in the form of The Ballad of Gay Tony . Supporting characters from the mainline game received some additional attention, including Luis Lopez, who became the player-controlled protagonist of this DLC. Yusuf Amir, a wealthy real estate developer and arrogant aristocrat, eventually rubs shoulders with Luis and leverages the leading man to perform outrageous tasks for him, including stealing an armed helicopter from an associate. What Yusuf wants, Yusuf gets. We're talking about a man who has lived in luxury since childhood and who continues to expend his father's fortune on sex, drugs, and the absurd.

Take this wild mission, for instance. During the “For the Man Who Has Everything” mission (aptly named), Yusuf decides that he wants a subway car as a decoration for his new Gulf property. This becomes, to be frank, one of the most ridiculous heists in Grand Theft Auto history. Luis must jump aboard the targeted train from an overpass. Without any choice in the matter, the player will enter 4- and 5-star wanted levels. The full force of the police department will be hot on your tail as you navigate to the front of the train. It's your job to then disconnect the car that will be stolen for Yusuf's property. Once you've done your job, Yusuf swoops in and whisks the car away in a helicopter. It's a rather intense mission that'll keep you on your toes to the very end.

Claude has one hell of a time in Liberty City, and his former beau, Catalina, doesn't make it any easier. Catalina is a well-known GTA antagonist first introduced in GTA III. But she also played a significant role in the game's prequel, GTA: San Andreas , where she and CJ worked together for a time, causing chaos along the West Coast. She'd eventually leave that all behind to embark on a Bonnie and Clyde lifestyle with Claude until she betrayed him for greater ambitions during the events of GTA III . Quickly, she becomes a thorn in the silent protagonist's side.

During the Kingdom Come mission provided by King Courtney, Claude is sent to pick up an Esperanto (vehicle) in the parking lot at Bedford Point. Upon arrival, Claude enters the vehicle only to find a note from Catalina alerting him to the fact that she's laid a trap for our anti-hero. She sends suicide bombers high on Spank (a fictional cocaine-like drug) to blow Claude to smithereens. It's a wild and unexpected turn during Claude's saga in Liberty City, and yet another betrayal on King Courtney's part. But the most disturbing part is that Courtney and Catalina were able to use people, hopped up on substances, to sacrifice their own skin and deliver an explosive demise to Claude.

GTA 5 contains some of the most unhinged moments in Grand Theft Auto history to date. This is partially thanks to Trevor and his penchant for impulsivity and possible psychopathy. However, during the events of GTA 5 , Michael and subsequently his cohorts Franklin and Trevor are under the FIB agency's thumb, or more specifically, Steven Haines' thumb. Haines is a man who is using his knowledge of Michael's involvement in a heist to coerce the crew into performing illicit tasks for his own gain. It's a relationship that is the foundation for many of the events that occur throughout GTA 5 .

During the “By the Book” mission, Haines invites Michael and Trevor to a warehouse where he instructs Michael to assassinate an Azerbaijani man by the name of Tahir Javan. The claim is simple: he's a known terrorist. The mission occurs in two parts. Michael must travel to the location of Javan and do the deed. But the initial location is proven to be a false lead. So, then the onus falls on Trevor, who must torture Javan's associate, Ferdinand Kerimov, to learn Javan's true location. This is where the “outrageous” and truly disturbing element comes into play. As a player taking control of Trevor, you get to perform the torture yourself. This includes waterboarding Kerimov, administering electrical shocks using a car battery, yanking teeth out with pliers, or beating the man with a wrench. It's a wild and dark twist that Trevor seems to revel in. The details are what make this sequence even more wickedly awful. Removing teeth clearly affects Kerimov's speech. You can even choose where you want to bludgeon the victim (knees, arms, stomach, etc.). It's absolutely horrific. But it's a moment that encapsulates Haines' manipulation and Trevor's depravity.

articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Shueisha Yu-Gi-Oh! is set to release a special version of Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine to celebrate its 30th anniversary, and has dropped a special trailer to help celebrate the occasion. articles.content:
Yu-Gi-Oh! has officially kicked off its 30th anniversary celebration in Japan with all sorts of special new events to commemorate the occasion , and Shonen Jump is going all out with a special version of the magazine featuring some of the biggest duels from the series' past. While this new edition of the magazine is unfortunately only going to be available in Japan for now, fans can see what the fuss is all about with a special trailer showing it off. You can check it out below.

As Yu-Gi-Oh! hits its 30th anniversary milestone , the franchise is going all out in Japan. “YU-GI-OH! ART WORKS” has been revealed as a special new art exhibition showing off the late Kazuki Takahashi's original work, but no potential international plans for it have been revealed as of this time. Though the franchise did have something else for everyone to enjoy with a new anime short directed by Eri Osada for KONAMI animation with Takahiro Kagami providing the character designs, and Haruka Taira serving as art director.

Yu-Gi-Oh! will also be releasing a special digital art book in Japan later this Fall to help cement this 30th anniversary, and while there's no international release planned for that either it's yet another fun way the franchise is returning. But it doesn't beat a potential return for the anime franchise as it's perfect for a remake anime series taking it on from the very beginning. With the franchise hitting this major milestone, it would be the perfect time to bring the classic anime back to the spotlight.

Yu-Gi-Oh! made a major pivot early into its run as Kazuki Takahashi shifted away from the darker death games seen in the earliest chapters to instead focus more on the trading card game battles the franchise would then be most well known for. This has made it such a massive hit over the decades that the anime would continue with a number of different iterations with new generations of stories and main characters playing their own versions of the card game from then on.

But while Yu-Gi-Oh! has found success with all of its other future generations that followed, the original series has remained in a stasis . Outside of coming back with a movie event, Yu-Gi-Oh! The Dark Side of Dimensions , back in 2016 to celebrate its 20th anniversary, the franchise is poised and ready for another new take. Though that might be tough without Takahashi around to oversee it. Can you believe it's been 30 years of Yu-Gi-Oh ? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

This time round, after months of increasingly intense speculation, the super spy's secret identity was finally unmasked on Instagram. Early Monday, the official 007 account began systematically deleting thousands of posts dating back almost a decade, mostly clips of previous films.

Just before 3 p.m. London time, a ten-second video was published, showing typed writing appearing over a black screen: "Identity Confirmed."

Then four minutes later, the long-awaited confirmation: a video of Pattinson — Robert Pattinson , clad in the traditional black dinner jacket and bow tie, his face half-obscured in shadow.

Variety understands that even as late as last week, many of Amazon 's own publicists were in the dark about the news, suggesting the announcement was hastily put together as speculation reached fever pitch.

With both Pattinson and director Denis Villeneuve about to embark on a press tour for "Dune 3" — and Pattinson also potentially embarking on Oscar campaigns for both "The Odyssey" and "Primetime" — it would have been impossible to hold one of the biggest secrets in entertainment any longer, let alone until there was a mutually convenient gap in both their schedules to appear at a splashy press conference in London and certainly not before year-end. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But breaking with the tradition of announcing a new Bond in a glamorous, British setting in favor of social media — which is younger-skewing and distinctly global — may also give fans a hint of what to expect now that the British secret agent is in the hands of an American tech company.

Amazon spent $8.5 billion buying MGM Studios in 2022 — primarily for the rights to Bond — and a further reported $1 billion last year to wrest creative control away from the Broccoli family, whose paterfamilias, Cubby Broccoli, launched the screen franchise in 1962 with "Dr. No."

Under the Broccolis — Cubby's daughter Barbara Broccoli and her stepbrother Michael Wilson have overseen Bond since 1995's "Goldeneye" — 007 became one of Britain's most iconic roles and one that usually went to a lesser-known actor. The idea was that no one performer should outshine the character himself. With Pattinson, who has led franchises including "Twilight" and "Batman," Amazon has upended that idea too.

articles.title: This Rare Star Wars Stormtrooper Costume Looks Nothing Like the Ones in the Movies, and That's What Makes It Special
articles.summary: You're going to need a lot of firepower if you're an imperial fascist regime determined to take over the galaxy. The Galactic Empire in Star Wars isn't shy to spend on TIE Fighters, AT-ATs, and even the planet destroying Death Star. While that's great, you'll need boots on the ground to be efficient in stamping […]
articles.content:
This set is one of only two in existence, created by Andrew Ainsworth, based on the original designs of legendary Star Wars concept artist Ralph McQuarrie. While the overall mold is similar to the Stormtrooper armor we saw in A New Hope and the rest of the original trilogy, the chrome color scheme is the most striking difference from the final version. However, it seems McQuarrie's idea of the troopers was very different from what George Lucas had in mind, as he also gave them high-tech shields, along with the franchise's most iconic weapon, the lightsaber. While the final version of the Stormtroopers were nameless grunts who couldn't hit the broad side of a barn, McQuarrie's version look like knights who would demolish the rebellion before it even began.

Just think back to how effective lightsabers have been in the Star Wars franchise, cutting through enemies like butter, thinning out numbers, and even rendering blast doors useless. Now imagine if every Stormtrooper in the Empire had one. Not only would they destroy the entire rebellion, but Luke would have not even left Tatooine. Eventually, Lucas probably decided that laser swords were too powerful to be wielded by regular soldiers, and made it so that only a small set of space wizards could use them. As for the chrome color scheme, as awesome as it would have looked, it was apparently very impractical to manufacture, especially back in 1977. However, we did get a glimpse of what it would look like thanks to Captain Phasma in 2015's The Force Awakens .

It's hard to think of Stormtroopers in any other color besides white. Sure, we've seen multiple variations over the years, like Deathtroopers and Shoretroopers, but it feels a bit wrong seeing the default Stormtrooper in anything but the traditional white. That's not to say that this chrome color scheme isn't amazing. I'd probably be saying the same thing if McQuarrie's original designs were approved. With only two of its kind in existence, this armor set gives us a glimpse at how different the Star Wars universe could have been if it wasn't for certain decisions. While it all worked out in the end, the new owner of this $16,250 suit of armor probably just found the centerpiece of their collection.

Would you have preferred if Star Wars Stormtrooper armor was chrome instead of white? Let us know in the comments!

articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Amid additional photography, Curry Barker ‘s Anything but Ghosts has brought on Matthew Lillard for a new role, Deadline has learned. Character details are being kept under wraps. Lillard joins a cast featuring Barker, Aaron Paul, Bryce Dallas Howard, Cooper Tomlinson and Violet McGraw. Tomlinson and Barker lead the film as wannabe ghost hunters who find themselves in over their heads as things spiral wildly and terrifyingly out of control. Barker is directing from a script co-written with frequent collaborator Tomlinson. The project reunites Focus Features , Blumhouse Atomic, Spooky Pictures and Divide/Conquer on the heels of his breakout horror phenomenon Obsession , which is now the top-grossing film in Focus Features' history at over $521 million worldwide. Focus, Blumhouse and Divide/Conquer are also partners on Occupant , the buzzy slasher from Josh Giuliano that releases January 15, 2027 after bowing out of TIFF. Slated for release on May 7, 2027, Anything but Ghosts is produced by Jason Blum (Blumhouse), Roy Lee & Steven Schneider (Spooky Pictures), Adam Hendricks & Greg Gilreath (Divide/Conquer), in association with Image Nation and That's a Bad Idea. Executive producers are Barker, Tomlinson and Image Nation's Ben Ross. Focus has worldwide rights on the film and Universal Pictures International will handle international distribution for the studio. Most recently seen starring in Mike Flanagan's series adaptation of Stephen King's Carrie for Amazon, Lillard will reteam with the filmmaker coming up on Rot , an indie horror film from director Alex Magistro that Flanagan is producing, as we first reported. Lillard previously worked with Flanagan on The Life of Chuck and has also recently been seen in Daredevil: Born Again and Prime Video's Cross , as well as Scream 7 . Next up, he'll be seen in Tony Gilroy's Searchlight flick Behemoth! , in theaters December 4, and James Gunn's Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow . He is repped by Verve, Strand Entertainment and Heller Law. articles.title: Kin in the Game: How the Rise of Family Office Investors Is Reshaping Media, Entertainment and Sports
articles.summary: The dawn of Skydance — the film and TV leviathan that came forth from the biggest media acquisition in 25 years — was enabled by the most influential trend in private investment in a decade: the rise of the family office investor. “Family office” is cuddly financial jargon for a specific form of holding company […]
articles.content:
The dawn of Skydance — the film and TV leviathan that came forth from the biggest media acquisition in 25 years — was enabled by the most influential trend in private investment in a decade: the rise of the family office investor.

"Family office" is cuddly financial jargon for a specific form of holding company that ultrarich people and their relatives rely on to manage their wealth. The proliferation of near billionaires — and billionaires proper — in the U.S. since the stock market boom began in the 1980s has led to the creation of thousands of well-endowed family offices. "The size of this is extraordinary," says Ian D'Souza, clinical professor of finance at the NYU Stern School of Business. "A lot of people don't realize just how big they are as an investor class in a global context and their different risk-return drivers.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Nobody Wants This' Renewed for Season 4 at Netflix Netflix’s 'Haunted Hotel' Renewed for Season 3

Family offices are gaining a level of clout that is having a profound impact on the ownership of media and entertainment assets. Many operate with a low profile — they don't have the same financial disclosure requirements as other companies and investment firms. Among the most powerful entities flexing financial muscle is Lawrence Investments, the office that handles the prodigious fortune amassed by 82-year-old Larry Ellison, co-founder of software giant Oracle. Ellison is the father of Skydance chairman and CEO David Ellison, the mastermind of Skydance's quest to bolt together studio and network assets.

The younger Ellison's one-two punch began last year with his $8 billion acquisition of Paramount and CBS. And then he went in dogged pursuit of Warner Bros., HBO, CNN, Discovery and numerous other channels. It all culminated in the closing of the $111 billion Warner Bros. Discovery transaction on Oct. 6. David Ellison couldn't have pulled off those head-spinning deals without the full faith and credit backing of the enormous Ellison family wealth held through Lawrence Investments, which has an estimated $160 billion in assets under management. But Ellison's empire-building boom has been financed with debt. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The enlarged Skydance is carrying $80 billion in red ink, and if Skydance doesn't make its aggressive debt and cost-reduction targets over the next three years, Larry Ellison will personally be on the hook for as much as $40 billion in debt payments to lenders. That's how far the software mogul, who recently became a major shareholder in the U.S. spinoff of TikTok, went to help finance his son's Hollywood ambition.

As demonstrated by the Ellison family's big swing, the influence of family office owners and investors will be markedly different from that of traditional private equity investors, experts say. Among the key differences:

According to data analysis from global investor research firm Altss, the number of family offices has grown at a rate of nearly 5% a year, culminating in more than 8,000 firms managing as much as $5 trillion or more in assets. The top 50 firms have an estimated $2.4 trillion in assets under management; the top 10 alone account for $1.5 trillion.

Generally speaking, it takes about $250 million in seed money to launch a large single-investor family office. Others are formed with $50 million to $100 million, and sometimes a handful of those firms will join together in a multi-family office. One of the biggest of those is Iconiq Capital, which handles some personal investing for Mark Zuckerberg, Sheryl Sandberg, Jack Dorsey and Linkedin co-founder Reid Hoffman, among others.

The reigning company among family offices remains Walton Enterprises, the $225 billion colossus controlled by the heirs of Walmart founder Sam Walton. Elon Musk, the entrepreneur behind Tesla and SpaceX, funnels some of his personal investments through his Excession family office, valued at $200 billion. Bill Gates' Cascade Investment is another heavyweight at $170 billion. Amazon pioneer Jeff Bezos holds his roughly 9% stake in the e-commerce giant (which encompasses Amazon MGM Studios and Prime Video) through his Bezos Expeditions office, with an estimated $107 billion in assets under management.

"The ability to create wealth over a short period of time right now is incredible, and because of that, all of a sudden you've got someone like Elon buying Twitter and turning it into what he wanted it to be," says Greg Suess, co-founder and head of Activist Artists Management's family office practice. "It was unfathomable that you would see an individual be able to buy a company of that size on his own. But that is the way it is now. A lot of these family offices are of the size where they can take swings on major entertainment assets. That has shocked the industry." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

At the same time, fortunes the size of Ellison's, Musk's and the Walton clan's are still outliers — the 1% of the 1%. The more pervasive impact is coming from the many other family offices steered by less than astronomically wealthy people who are drawn to the soft power of media. Think Steve Sarowitz, the payroll-software billionaire whose Illinois-based 4S Bay Partners family office teamed with Justin Baldoni to launch "It Ends With Us" production company Wayfarer Studios.

David Steward II has also inherited significant wealth from his father, World Wide Technology co-founder David Steward. The younger Steward in recent years has invested in comic-book imprints and the Lion Forge Entertainment animation studio with the goal of bringing more diverse stories to life as family animation films. The Steward family has also worked with NASCAR and Richard Petty Motorsports to sponsor the groundbreaking driver Bubba Wallace, and it was an owner of the family's hometown NHL team, the St. Louis Blues, from 2012 until selling the stake in 2024.

"Our mission is very much around what we call diverse stories authentically told. It's about displaying and telling stories from varied backgrounds, whether it be racial, socioeconomic or gender," the younger Steward says. "We're a lot more patient with outcomes because we have a higher vision. We're not only investing to get a return; we're investing for change. We're investing in people at the end of the day. So it's a different kind of philosophy as we look at those things.

"There are three pillars to any family office that I've ever been around," says Edward Hamati, a wealth management pro who is chief investment officer for the Steward Trust and the Steward Family Office. "Trust, treasury and banking — that's one bucket. Building the corpus, that's another bucket. Anyone can give you 50 ways that you do that. And then there's the third bucket, which is, What is this family about and what do we have to care about because of the family? What are they motivated by? What do the kids want? Is there a lot of family politics? You have to think through all that around any family you work with."

Joe Becher, CAA's global managing partner and founder of its executive search practice, has felt the same demand that spurred Suess and partners to form Activist. Becher expanded CAA into family office specialty services as he found himself conducting C-suite searches for firms that had been bought out by family offices. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Probably two to three years ago we started seeing this trend of family offices popping up everywhere, whether it be in media companies or music-catalog businesses or sports franchises," Becher says. "Very often, instead of us dealing with an owner in isolation or a private equity firm with institutional capital, we were dealing with family offices. They needed our help to understand the assets that they've invested in. They needed our help to structure them the right way and build the right operating teams."

Traditionally, the family office investment model was associated with vintage American family fortunes such as the oil money of the Rockefellers or the publishing and media empires of William Randolph Hearst and E.W. Scripps. Hearst and Scripps still operate as well-established media companies. But their governance structure makes them essentially family offices that are run by trusted staffers who ensure that the generational wealth keeps flowing to heirs for decades to come.

But nothing has animated the family office sector lately like the availability of sports teams and music catalogs. The latter is seen as a form of timeless physical media that will retain value no matter how much music consumption changes in the streaming era. On the other hand, sports franchise deals are usually driven by raw passion and bragging rights.

"There's only so many of them, and so that sense of paying for scarcity and legacy impact are important drivers for family offices that don't really exist for other types of pooled capital because they have a time-duration problem," D'Souza says. Some first-generation wealth generators thrive on the challenge of turning around properties like sports teams or rehabilitating beloved fashion or retail brands. "They feel like, ‘I made it once; I can do it again,'" says D'Souza, who has served as a board member for numerous family offices over the years.

At best, a family office can bring to the table resources and in some cases synergies with other holdings for an acquisition. Steward II notes that the company's work with NASCAR and driver Wallace led to World Wide Technology upgrading the racing circuit's digital infrastructure to help it make the most of AI and other cutting-edge tech.

Steward II emphasizes that the company can't completely ignore financial results. But it has the luxury of options. "We do have the investments that are a little bit colder and distant and more financially oriented. And then we have this entrepreneurial pile, and in that pile comes [ideas] by way of passion and by way of utilizing the relationships that we have," Steward says. "Everything we've done in sports and entertainment has been led by those two things. We want to see change in the industry as well. So how can we best not only put our creative foot forward, but how can we leverage our relationships for change as well?" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The flood of investment and financing dollars flowing into a broad range of industry deals in recent years has turned the private investment vehicles of the ultra-high-net-worth crowd into the most courted players in global investing. "It has become recognized that families are more viable owners of various assets than they were considered to be in the past," Activist's Suess says. "The wealth has grown so much. They've become business rock stars."

(Pictured top: Family office investors Gigi Pritzker, Steve Sarowitz, David Steward II and François-Henri Pinault)

articles.title: 5 DC Legacy Heroes Who Deserve a Shot With Their Mentor’s Mantles, Including a Controversial Batman Sidekick
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics DC Comics introduced us to the superhero in 1938 and two years later, we'd get the first legacy sidekick in the form of Robin. The inclusion of the sidekick meant down the road legacy would become an important part of the DC Multiverse. Over the years, legacy has been one of the defining features of […]
articles.content:
The DC superhero community consists of numerous superhero families. In these families, there are characters that we all expect to end up in the big seat – for example, Dick Grayson becoming Batman or Jon Kent becoming Superman down the road. However, there are other members of these families that we never expect to graduate to the big mantle. This is unfair to some of them, as they definitely deserve their chance in the spotlight. These five DC legacy heroes deserve their time with their mentor's mantles, including the most controversial member of the Bat-Family.

Wonder Girl is the most confusing mantle in comics . The first Wonder Girl is Donna Troy, but it was also a teen Diana. See, originally, Wonder Girl was the equivalent of Superboy. This was changed for the Teen Titans, leading to the creation of Donna Troy. Wonder Girl would become the sidekick of Wonder Woman and eventually, Donna would be replaced by Cassie Sandsmark (who in turn would be replaced by Yara Flor). Diana has been replaced as Wonder Woman a few times over the years, with both Artemis and Donna taking her place.

Cassie is basically the forgotten Wonder Girl, but she deserves her chance as Wonder Woman. Her journey as a hero in the mid '00s showed off just how great she could be. She became the center of the Teen Titans and even led the group, growing as a person and discovering the truth about her parentage. Cassie fell from grace for a while because of the New 52, so she needs a little more seasoning, but in the long run, she should be the next Wonder Woman.

“Death of Superman” shocked the world, with the first superhero's demise reported by the evening news. After “Funeral for a Friend” and “World Without a Superman”, we got “Reign of the Supermen”, a story that introduced four replacements for the Man of Steel, including John Henry Irons. John built a special suit of armor to protect the people of Suicide Slum, eventually battling against Cyborg Superman alongside Superboy, the Eradicator, and the one true Superman. They won and John became Steel, fighting alongside the Superman Family, joining the Justice League, and becoming an elder statesman of the superhero community.

Superman has been put out of commission several times over the years and Steel deserves his shot as the one true Superman. He's a great hero, having fought against the biggest threats in DC history. Sure, he doesn't have superpowers, but he has the next best things – intelligence. He would be a different kind of Superman for sure, but that's the fun of legacy heroes.

Steel wasn't the only awesome addition of “Reign of the Supermen” , there was also Conner Kent. Conner was a clone of Superman created by Project Cadmus (it would eventually be revealed that Lex Luthor's DNA was used to stabilize his genes to allow for him to be viable) to replace Superman in case he died. After Superman's death at Doomsday's hands, the Newsboy Legion freed the teen clone to fight for Metropolis, leading to him becoming one of the four Supermen. He'd eventually become the new Superboy, becoming a legend in his own right, founding Young Justice, and helping re-establish the Teen Titans, giving his life to save the multiverse in Infinite Crisis before being resurrected in the 31st century.

Conner Kent was almost destroyed by the New 52 (the saga of Superboy during the New 52 is one of the most mystifying of them all, especially since Conner was having a renaissance pre-New 52), but he's since come been brought back to prominence. He's still played as the impulsive younger hero and it's about time that he got a promotion. Making him the Superman for a time would be perfect for him and entertaining for readers.

Green Arrow is one of those heroes who was created to take advantage of the success of Batman. Back in the Golden Age, Oliver Queen was a rich playboy who decided to become a superhero after a tragedy, except in his case, he went with Robin Hood instead of bats. He had it all – the Arrowcave, the Arrowcar, the gimmick weapons – and he also had the sidekick: Roy Harper. As Speedy, he would become one of the premiere teen heroes, joining the Teen Titans, and would have his own drug addiction story. He'd end up becoming Arsenal and Red Arrow, but has never taken Ollie's place.

Roy Harper becoming Red Arrow was cool, but it's long past time he actually got to become Green Arrow. Even the Absolute Universe wouldn't make Roy the Green Arrow. Roy has been through a lot over the decades and the best way to show that he has grown beyond all of that is for him to step into the mantle of Green Arrow. It's an important part of the evolution of every legacy character and it's one that Roy needs.

DC has never known what to do with Jason Todd . This started back at the beginning. Dick Grayson was getting popular as a Teen Titan and it was hard to explain how he was in New York with Titans and patrolling Gotham with Bats every night. So, they made Jason, but instead of making him an actual an all-new character, they just copied Dick's origin, changing the serial numbers, and left it at that. Fans were indifferent but then post- Crisis , they would create the mouthy, angry version and fans hated him even more, leading to his death in “Death of the Family”. He'd eventually be resurrected as the villainous Red Hood, before returning to heroism and becoming the black sheep of the Bat-Family.

Red Hood was a villain when Batman died and tried to become a villainous Dark Knight, losing out to Dick Grayson. Since then, he's back to being a hero but DC can never come up with anything for him to do long-term. He's a character without a rudder and it's long past time that he got the chance to become Batman. While they could make him a violent failure like Azrael had been, it would be more interesting to see him actually successful. You could do an excellent Jason Todd as Batman story and it's about time that DC stopped being cowards.

What DC legacy heroes do you think should take over their mentor's mantles? Disagree with any of my choices? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: 2025 Sega Game Permanently Delisted From All Platforms
articles.summary: A 2025 Sega game has been permanently removed from sale on all platforms, meaning it is no longer available to purchase in any capacity. Those who own it will retain access to it, though. This delisting impacts PlayStation, PC, Xbox, and Nintendo gamers because the game is available on PS5, PC, Xbox Series X, and […]
articles.content:
Those who are Football Manager fans will know that Football Manager 26 was a low point for the series, as evidenced by its 68 on Metacritic and its low user review scores across the Internet. To this end, perhaps it should come as no surprise that a year after its release, developer Sports Interactive and publisher Sega were happy to blink it from the Internet once it was replaced by Football Manager 27 last week. For the sake of comparison, Football Manager 27 has an 80 on Metacritic and far more positive user review scores as well.

That said, this is a pattern for the series, and no doubt has to do with expiring licenses more than embarrassment from an underwhelming installment. That said, back in the day these licenses were signed for longer, so games wouldn't delist so quickly. In an era of annualization, though, the agreements are getting shorter and shorter.

A Worrying Trend Interestingly, Football Manager 26 was available via subscription services up until its delisting, and these contracts will play out. To this end, it remains available to PS Plus Extra and PS Plus Premium subscribers, but this will stop being the case on November 16.

Unfortunately, for Football Manager fans, this also prevents users with tighter budgets from picking up older games when they are replaced, and thus become very cheap to acquire. This is how it used to work, at least. Given the incremental changes each installment makes, there's not a ton of benefit to owning the latest Football Manager compared to an installment four years ago. Further, sometimes the new instalment is not good, like Football Manager 26 itself. All of this is to say, the practice of these one-year delistings doesn't benefit anyone other than the publishers cutting the checks for these licensing agreements.

At the moment of publishing, neither Sports Interactive nor Sega have commented on the delisting, and for a variety of reasons, we do not expect this to change. If it does, though, we will update the story accordingly.

Interestingly, this follows another, more high-profile delisting from Sega last month, which saw it delist a brand new 2026 game only days after release . Meanwhile, in other recent Sega news, a remake of a 1980s Sega game is now available on Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 for just $4 .

Garfield is a new animated series coming to Paramount+ on December 11th, and returns the animated cat to his 2D roots with a slate of designs that look as close to Davis' comics as fans could hope for after the franchise's most recent CG animated outing unfortunately failed to meet expectations . But with this new take on the franchise reviving the TV series for a new era, you can check out the first look at the new Garfield below ahead of its streaming launch.

Garfield will be making its streaming debut with Paramount+ on December 11th. It has yet to confirm how many episodes is debut season will be running for, but all episodes will be launching with the streaming service at the same time. Paramount is going to be counting down to the premiere of the new animated series beginning on Monday, November 23rd with “I Hate Mondays,” a series of shorts featuring this new take on the icon releasing with the NickToons YouTube channel to give fans an idea of what to expect.

This new take on Garfield has been created by Dave H. Johnson and John Trabbic III for Nickelodeon Animation Studios with Adrian Younge and Ali Shaheed Muhammad (of A Tribe Called Quest) composing the music. The new version of the famous feline will be voiced by Emmy award winning star Lamorne Morris (who was most recently seen in action with Spider-Noir), and thankfully this version of Garfield is communicating through his thoughts alone like the comics rather than openly speaking like seen with some adaptations.

Garfield ‘s new animated outing will feature a stacked voice cast including Joe Brogie as Jon Arbuckle, co-creator Dave H. Garfield moves the titular cat and Jon to the big city, but makes sure to keep the icon's “sarcasm, selfishness, and unapologetic laziness” from Jim Davis' original comics as teased by the series' press release. This first look trailer sees how he has adapted to newer technologies, but hopefully keeps the spirit intact without going too far in that direction for its stories.

We'll see for ourselves soon enough, but how are you feeling about this new Garfield animated series so far? What do you think of this first look? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: 'The Odyssey' Cinematographer Hoyte Van Hoytema Breaks Down Filming Climactic Thunderstorm Scene in Imax
articles.summary: Christopher Nolan shot “The Odyssey” to be experienced on the biggest screen possible so audiences could feel the full impact and be fully immersed in that experience — so everything was shot practically. One of the most challenging sequences to pull off was the film’s final storm scene as Matt Damon’s Odysseus faces the wrath […]
articles.content:
Christopher Nolan shot " The Odyssey " to be experienced on the biggest screen possible so audiences could feel the full impact and be fully immersed in that experience — so everything was shot practically.

One of the most challenging sequences to pull off was the film's final storm scene as Matt Damon's Odysseus faces the wrath of Poseidon and the full force of Zeus. It was to be climactic and intense, and Odysseus loses all his men as a result of the final insult to the gods. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Maya Jama Strikes Deal With Netflix (EXCLUSIVE) 'Big Mistakes' Season 2 Casts Randall Park, Debi Mazar, T.R. Knight, Jeff Perry

"We had been talking about going out there to sea, sit on real boats and shoot on Imax," cinematographer Hoyte Van Hoytema explains.

A large amount of the film was shot on the open ocean, where Nolan, his cast and crew spent four months capturing how hard the journey would have been as they endured crashing waves. And while the climactic moment ended up being shot in Los Angeles, Nolan didn't spare any expense in pulling off the sequence, relying instead on old-fashioned filmmaking. Speaking with Variety for Inside the Frame , Van Hoytema explains the scene provided a challenge: "How to replicate something and make it feel visceral and real? How can we do that and avoid a huge amount of CG?" Two decommissioned jet engines were used as wind machines. Van Hoytema's chief lighting technician and gaffer Adam Chambers built light boxes that would emulate thunder and lightning. The boat was then put on a gimbal, all while being shot on an Imax camera. "It was like shooting a real storm, just under safety supervision," Van Hoytema says. He adds, "We did a lot of different setups in that whole scene. It is designed to feel extremely chaotic; it's designed to sort of not understand really what's going on." The lighting design was something he also had to think about. "It was interesting because I was thinking, if you're out at sea at night 2,000 years ago, without electricity and you end up in a thunderstorm, what would that feel like? I was thinking, if you can see everything around you, that's going to look fake."

A CGI storm didn't feel right because the entire crew had been meticulous about keeping everything as grounded and as experiential as possible. Van Hoytema says the team built overhead lighting rigs that were approximately 60×30 feet, hanging on cranes above the ship. "It meant that you would see flashes that progressively move from behind them to the front of them, as it opens up the sky. "What you see is short bursts and there's just darkness or a little bit of a glow. It's like trying to see this relentless endless sea, this weather, this saltwater and they're just so close to death. It's extremely claustrophobic at the same time."

When it came to framing Odysseus, Van Hoytema was wired in to keep him in place on the gimbal. His Imax camera on his shoulder was also wired in.

"I was not trying to be in any way precious about framing whatsoever. I was just trying through with a jet engine blowing, gallons of water in my face. I was literally just trying to identify if it was even Matt Damon in the shot. It was extremely visceral, and it's almost hard to grasp. It was not a situation in which you could just start a take or not. Every take was an event." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Van Hoytema says the camera starts to roll and the jet engines start. "They rise, and at some point, they sound like two fighter jets are next to your ear. And it gets really wild because they start moving the gimbal as well, and you're holding on for your life. The camera gets turned; it's the original Imax camera, not the blimp and the Imax camera is very loud. However, in that situation, you don't even know if it's turned on. You do a take, and you have a crazy powerful adrenaline rush."

In contrast, Van Hoytema recalled a moment when the crew was out to sea, in open waters and a pod of bottlenose dolphins appeared. It was completely unplanned.

Van Hoytema recalls, "It's interesting because it was also pretty violent that day. It was very harsh weather and I remember a lot of people on the crew got seasick. As we started filming, dolphins started to jump out of the water. What is interesting is that it symbolizes that no matter what the weather does, we take the weather as it comes and accept it as the reality you work in that day."

articles.content:
John Summit blasted the Grammys on Monday morning after the popular DJ didn't earn any nominations this year, posting a tweet calling the awards “a fucking joke” and vowing he won't submit again unless the Recording Academy institutes significant changes.

“I'm not just talking about myself either there's zero respect for real electronic dance music & dj's,” Summit said. “The whole dance category is just music industry fueled pop stars.”

This year's nominees for best dance/electronic recording are Madonna, Fred Again.., Slayyyter , Tame Impala, Tinashe and underscores. In a follow-up post, Summit wrote that he was “not saying the artists nominated aren't good, they're just not dance music, they're pop.”

“No dj is playing that music in the clubs,” he said.

To some extent, Summit's gripes reflect a more widespread critique within the dance categories and how it's converged with more mainstream pop. In 2023, the Recording Academy launched a new category, best pop dance recording, as a means of giving more mainstream acts a spot for recognition while opening up more of the field for traditional DJs.

Summit isn't the first act to air his gripes at the Grammys and decide to boycott the Academy altogether. The Weeknd, for instance, famously boycotted the awards for years after his album After Hours was snubbed. He ended his boycott during the Grammy Awards in 2025.

articles.title: I'm Glad Even Chris Pratt Is Talking Guardians Of The Galaxy Now James Gunn's Schedule Is Wide Open
articles.summary: Somebody check if Feige still has James Gunn's number.
articles.content:
I thought I'd made peace with saying goodbye to James Gunn 's Guardians of the Galaxy . The third movie wrapped things up beautifully, and with Gunn running DC Studios, I figured there wasn't much chance of getting the old gang back together. Well, Hollywood has a funny way of changing plans. Gunn is leaving his leadership position at DC , and Chris Pratt is already talking about the possibility of making another Guardians movie with him. Let me just state for the record that I'm right there with him.

Well, now I want it too. Gunn spent nearly a decade building one of Marvel's strangest superhero teams into something audiences genuinely cared about. Somehow, he also made me cry over a talking raccoon more times than I'd care to admit.

Pratt's comments are especially interesting because he previously had some pretty specific thoughts about returning as Star-Lord. Last year, I covered his concerns about finding somebody who could fill Gunn's shoes . At the time, it seemed unlikely the filmmaker would ever be available. Suddenly, that possibility doesn't sound quite so ridiculous.

articles.title: How Netflix‘s Animated 'Steps’ Reimagines the Cinderella Story Through the Eyes of Her Asian Stepsisters and Finds a New Kind of Happily Ever After
articles.summary: Netflix’s animated feature “Steps” surface reboots the Cinderella tale: an orphan tormented by an evil stepmother and her loathsome daughters. But this tale, directed by Alyce Tzue and John Ripa, turns that legend upside-down, offering a revisionist history of what really happened — and it has nothing to do with horrible steps, but everything to […]
articles.content:
Netflix 's animated feature " Steps " surface reboots the Cinderella tale: an orphan tormented by an evil stepmother and her loathsome daughters. But this tale, directed by Alyce Tzue and John Ripa, turns that legend upside-down, offering a revisionist history of what really happened — and it has nothing to do with horrible steps, but everything to do with fear, othering and mean girls, with some magic of course.

Set in the kingdom of Alouette, the story begins with two little girls, Lilith and Margot, moving into their stepfather's home and becoming fast friends with his little girl, Cinderella. Everybody's happy until Cinderella sides with the mean girls at a party, and their father dies. Lilith turns rebellious, because why not? The whole town kinda hates her because she's different anyway — she, Margot and mom are Asian. Blonde Cinderella talks to animals, cleans, sings and everyone loves her. But while the story follows the familiar contours — there's a fairy godmother and a prince, of course — "Steps" takes many twists in an entertaining and illuminating journey. Film's voice cast stars Ali Wong, Amanda Seyfried, Stephanie Hsu, Bette Midler, Daniel Radcliffe, Young Manzino and Nikki Glaser. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories James Bond Shocker: Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult Late Contenders for 007 After Auditioning for Denis Villeneuve Amazon MGM Studios Japan 'Doubling' Investment to Meet Global Standards, Local Chief Buddy Marini Reveals at Tokyo Market

The first animated feature from Amy Poehler's Paper Kite, the film looks luscious, like a tempting birthday cake or candy.

Tzue had been working on the film for seven years. Comedians and writers Ricki Lindhome and Kate Micucci of Garfunkel and Oates had a concept that they worked together on with Paper Kite, says Tzue, and brought it to Netflix. "There was this idea of a movie from the stepsisters' perspective. It was a very different movie," says the director. "They were white stepsisters, and they were more the canonically mean girls that you might expect and they sent the script to me to check it out. And I thought it had just like this sharply feminist message, and as well as these values of inclusivity and sisterhood that really grabbed me. And so I pitched to both Paper Kite and Netflix, and I got the job to direct it." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But Tzue saw parallels to her young life in the story as the film took a different direction.

"I will say that my Taiwanese and Chinese ethnicity is a deep part of who I am, and it has made me into the artist and filmmaker that I am. I'm proud of it, and growing up in a pretty homogeneous small town, it has also caused me to feel different," she says. "And I think one being making the stepsisters Asian allowed me to give them this nuance and specificity and vulnerability that can be informed from my own experience."

She adds: "I felt like there were just these parallels between my experience and Lilith's experience. Just like Cinderella fits this archetype of a fairy tale protagonist, and Lilith doesn't. I also felt like the girls I grew up with were, you know, meant to find this traditional kind of happiness and they're happy ever after. And I felt like I was too different to find that myself. It was this effort to tell stories about what I know and the personal journey that I'm so close to."

Tzue says, "My directing partner John Ripa and I feel like we will have done our jobs if even one person walks away feeling like they can stand up for someone else."

Veteran animator Ripa joined the production a little later than Tzue, but they immediately vibed on the film's themes. He wanted to find out "what she wanted to say with it because what she wanted to say comes from her experiences growing up and talking about wanting everybody to see themselves in the fairy tale, everybody deserving a happy happily ever after and the idea of empathy and kindness. And for me, I felt like that was very universal. And I felt like that was really important, especially in the world today. And so, I really locked into what Alice wanted to say with it and that was kind of like my driving force too."

The Rococo Alouette was also a character. "This kingdom of conformists that wouldn't accept any difference, right? And we wanted to play into that idea as well," she says

There's original songs, lots of gags — including one about the prince's face blindness — scary villain chases and of course, a glass carriage and slippers.

She quips that Cinderella purists might not like this version of the story but she and the team had "fun of playing around with fairy tale tropes, trying to see what world lies beyond this kingdom of Alouette. There's an enchanted forest, and also comes with it these trolls that live under bridges and ride motorcycles, but really, I think what we're trying to do is bring it thematically back to this idea of who's included in the fairy tale and who isn't. You know, in our world, the trolls aren't, which gives ‘Steps' this room to grow into or it gives Alouette room to grow into the kingdom that we kind of wish it were by the end." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The look is bright, saturated color, gleaming and dreamy. It almost looks toylike. The animators' intent was to draw in the audience with the colors and the miniaturization.

"I come from a CG background, and I've loved working with CG as a 3D medium in particular," Tzue, who started out as an architect, says. "From architecture to working as a CG generalist, I've loved things like surfacing and lighting and while I love the movies that have 3D emulate 2D — they look beautiful — I really wanted to push 3D to feel even more 3D."

"Especially in terms of the world, the fabrics, the textures, just how kind of rich and ornate and how everything was kind of really constructed. It was like a big part of the look of the film that you know we wanted to do because it's one of the things that CG does best," says Ripa. "It can add these textures and freckles and to this ornate Rococo world. But then you have to take it and make sure that the audience is seeing and feeling what they're supposed to see and feel, because if you let it take over, you can lose emotion in connection with the characters. So, we were trying to make sure, even in the complexity of it, that the characters and the emotions were still at the at the forefront."

articles.title: Berlin Winner Tatiana Huezo Close to Completing Road Movie ‘Galerna’ Following Awards Boost: ‘I’m Dying to Finish It’
articles.summary: Mexican-Salvadoran director Tatiana Huezo is inching close to finishing “Galerna,” her follow-up to the Berlinale-winning documentary “The Echo.” The film, which has been brewing for the last three years, is fresh off market wins at both San Sebastián and Morelia, giving the director a major boost ahead of her time at IDFA as this year’s […]
articles.content:
Mexican-Salvadoran director Tatiana Huezo is inching close to finishing "Galerna," her follow-up to the Berlinale-winning documentary "The Echo." The film, which has been brewing for the last three years, is fresh off market wins at both San Sebastián and Morelia, giving the director a major boost ahead of her time at IDFA as this year's Guest of Honor.

Speaking with Variety out of the Amsterdam festival and following a lengthy career discussion moderated by IDFA artistic director Isabel Arrate Fernandez, Huezo says her second fiction film (following 2021's lauded "Prayers for the Stolen") feels like a "breached child." It's a film that was stopped for a little while due to lack of financing, and I call it a breached child because the culmination of this filmmaking journey, the premiere, feels like a birth. It's like seeing a child be born and finally walking alone." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Bill Skarsgård Says He ‘Wasn’t Even Thrown Into the Mix’ to Be James Bond: ‘Maybe They Were Like, “We Can’t Do a Swede”’ Pierce Brosnan Approves of Callum Turner as James Bond: He's 'So Strong' and I'm 'Eager to See' Who Becomes the Next 007

"Galerna" trails casting directors Lúa (Ilse Salas) and Noé (Lázaro Gabino Rodríguez), whose latest job is to find natural actors for a sci-fi movie. They are working together for the first time, with Noé coming from the countryside and Lúa an unemployed actress from the big city. The duo travels together to remote areas in Mexico, staying in the houses of welcoming strangers along the way. In this road trip, they encounter a country that simultaneously embraces them and makes them confront their fears and prejudices.

"This film was held up because we took the risk of shooting without consolidated financing," adds the director. "We were also very dependent on the weather and several other uncontrollable circumstances." "Galerna" was shot in Juchitán in the South of Mexico and the northern desert of Chihuahua. "It's a journey, a road movie." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Asked about why she decided to take "Galerna" to several markets over the last two years, Huezo emphasizes both the financial aspect of meeting investors and the possibility of getting peer feedback. "We had the opportunity to go to San Sebastián's works-in-progress showcase to look for money. I was very apprehensive because you don't ever know what you have until you share it with others. I am always very afraid. Every time I make a film, it feels like the first time."

"Every film is a leap into the void, where you have to reinvent yourself, considering all the risks involved and relying on a deep desire to tell a story," she goes on. "That's how I experience filmmaking. I never take on a project where I can say everything is perfectly under control and I know exactly what the results will be. For me, every film is incredibly intense, and I never know how it will turn out."

The director notes how "financing independent cinema is always difficult." "It's important to mention that the primary source of funding for this film comes from EFICINE, a state fund that supports Mexican independent cinema. It has been absolutely essential. Without that support, Mexican cinema simply wouldn't exist. Thanks to the fund, we were able to get the initial phase of production underway, but this is a very complex and ambitious film."

But the real "turning point" for "Galerna" was being part of San Sebastián's WIP Latam section. "The film resonated beautifully with people there. It stirred deep emotions and sparked a great deal of curiosity."

"Galerna" won the coveted EGEDA Platino Industria Award worth €30,000 ($33,000) at the festival, which the director credits with drawing the interest of other investors and distributors. Right after the festival, Mexico's Sula Films boarded the project, joining Pimienta Films ("Roma") as a co-producer.

"It was a realization that the film was alive," she says. Huezo then took the project to Mexico's Morelia Film Festival, where it snagged the top prize at Impulso Morelia, the WIP section of the event. "The film really took off from there, thankfully, and reaffirmed my belief that these leaps into the unknown are absolutely worth taking." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Right now, we're in the final stages of production," she says. "I'm here at [IDFA], caught in a whirlwind with a packed schedule, while simultaneously navigating the very intense final push to complete the film. I'm working with musicians, the sound designer, and finalizing the edit. It's all coming together in a great swirl of activity to bring ‘Galerna' to life. I'm dying to finish it and finally bring this child of mine into the world."

Lastly, the filmmaker briefly spoke about the "wonderful" sense of hope brought to Latin American politics following Lula's presidential victory in Brazil last month. "Lula's victory was like a brilliant light at the end of a dark tunnel; it brought a major shift in perspective in Latin America. It signalled that we are still here; we still have the possibility of resisting, of fighting for democracy together."

"There was this heavy sense of darkness blanketing the entire world, a wave of fascism, the rise of the far-right, something truly formidable and profoundly dark," she adds. "I feel that Lula's victory shifted the landscape in a very significant way, not just in Mexico but globally. There are crazy, deranged people in power today in Latin America. People who are extremely dangerous and who are completely and utterly removed from anything human, but right now, I'm feeling hopeful."
