Rivkin will oversee physical production for Shondaland. Prior to joining the company, she worked at Michael Ellenberg's Media Res for four years, where she also oversaw physical production on shows like “The Morning Show” for Apple TV. Prior to that, she worked in the Netflix original series, drama, group as well as at Legendary Entertainment.

Smith-Forge will lead development of new series at Shondaland under their expansive overall deal with Netflix. She was most recently the president of Don Cheadle's production company, This Radicle Act Productions. She was also previously senior vice president of production for Berlanti Productions.

Shondaland has been based at Netflix since 2017. It was announced over the summer that the company would remain at the streamer for a further five years. In addition to serving as the exclusive home to Shondaland film and TV projects, the overall deal also covers gaming, merchandise, and live events connected to the IP.

Shondaland's biggest show to date on Netflix is "Bridgerton," which aired its fourth season earlier this year and is currently prepping its fifth. Along with the previous prequel about Queen Charlotte, Netflix recently greenlit a second “Bridgerton” prequel about a young Lady Violet.

" The Navigator ," a voyaging film directed by Jordan Manley and executive produced by Harrison Ford , has unveiled an exclusive clip ahead of its Nov. 19 East Coast bow at DOC NYC.

Ford also supplied a message with the clip.

"‘The Navigator' is a deeply moving film – one I'm truly grateful for. Its powerful storytelling and cinematic beauty left me in awe. Master navigator Nainoa Thompson, his teachers, and his students are extraordinary examples of profound humility. They help us understand why ancient wisdom matters in a modern world, and remind us what we are capable of when we act in harmony with nature," Ford said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Dune 3' Cast Says the Movie Takes 'Departures' From the Books, but 'You're Crazy If You’re Going to Pick Fault' With It 'The Odyssey' Oscar Campaign Kicks Off With 8 New Revelations, From Tom Holland’s Shorter Skirt to Pattinson’s Rejected Wig and a Trojan Horse Stuck in Customs

Ford is one of seven executive producers on the project, a group that also includes Yvon Chouinard and Laurene Powell Jobs. Kathy Thompson and Laura Yale are the producers, and Yo-Yo Ma contributes cello to a score by Matthew Robert Cooper.

The film's world premiere took place Oct. 21 at Hawaiʻi Theater on Oʻahu during the Hawaii International Film Festival, and it left with the Pacific Awards – Feature prize. Thompson, meanwhile, received the Halekulani Legacy Award.

In 1980, Thompson crossed from Hawai'i to Tahiti by voyaging canoe using neither a compass nor modern instruments, becoming the first Native Hawaiian to do so in six centuries.

Now nearly 50 years later, he is making the crossing again, for what the film presents as the last time. Thompson sails with a handful of student navigators. They rely on the stars, natural cues and the lessons of the late Mau Piailug, a master navigator, along a 2,400-mile route their ancestors sailed. Piailug, who was raised on Satawal in Micronesia, taught Native Hawaiians traditional navigation. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Manley said in a director's statement: "I came to see a deep burden and ‘kuleana' that rests upon the shoulders of Nainoa Thompson, who has spent the last 50 years of his life fulfilling a promise made to his teacher, Micronesian master navigator Mau Piailug, to prevent navigation from going extinct."

Joe Bob Briggs ' "The Last Drive-in" is coming to an end at Shudder this year, but he's taking a bold new step that will thrill genre fans.

Briggs, along with distributor and producer Bob Berney, announced the creation of Coney Island Pictures today, Variety can exclusively reveal. The horror-focused production and distribution company will have worldwide distribution from Picturehouse , Berney's distribution and marketing company. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'The Odyssey' Oscar Campaign Kicks Off With 8 New Revelations, From Tom Holland’s Shorter Skirt to Pattinson’s Rejected Wig and a Trojan Horse Stuck in Customs Tom Holland Says Starring in 'The Odyssey' Has Given Him an 'Ambition to See What Else Is Out There for Me'

"I've known Bob since the '80s, when the two of us were rooming together at the Cannes Film Festival to save money and collaborating on weird film festivals at the only real arthouse in Dallas," Briggs said in a statement. "Bob went off to Hollywood, distributed the two most successful indie films in history, marketed movies worth a billion in box office, many of them winning Academy Awards, and developed friendships with the top directors in the business, while I was writing books about exploitation movies and hosting ‘The Night Evelyn Came Out of the Grave' at 1 a.m. on cable. Our two worlds eventually collided through what I call the Horror Renaissance of 2016. Bob's friend Guillermo del Toro won the Academy Award, and AMC Networks launched the Shudder streaming service, where I would spend almost a decade putting the trivia embedded in the back of my brain to work."

"I've known Joe Bob since I owned the Inwood Theater and he was the film critic at the Dallas Times Herald," Berney, Picturehouse's CEO, also said in a statement. "Together, in the early '90s, we screened both classic and unknown genre films with special guest stars and tributes. The status of horror has been greatly elevated in today's marketplace, and Coney Island Pictures is uniquely situated to acquire and produce a new generation of films with the added advantage of being able to talk directly to the fans of Joe Bob Briggs. It's something we've always wanted to do and the time is right." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Per the presser, Coney Island's first projects include "a dark horror comedy, a new version of a classic horror paperback, and a reimagining of the 1981 cult horror classic ‘ Basket Case ' in collaboration with original director Frank Henenlotter."

Anthony Sneed, Henenlotter's longtime creative partner and protégé, will direct the adaptation.

"I sponsored the world premiere of the original ‘Basket Case' at the Highway 183 Drive-In in Irving, Texas," Briggs also said. "Bob helped me promote it with the World Drive-In Movie Festival. Now, decades later, we're working with its original creator, Frank Henenlotter. Because every generation needs a ‘Basket Case!'"

Berney and Briggs will serve as co-CEOs of the company. Picturehouse's Jeanne R. Berney will serve as head of marketing, and former Explorers Club media executive Austin Raywood will serve as head of production.

Briggs is best known for his decades of presenting and discussing horror films on television. His show "Joe Bob's Drive-in Theater" aired on The Movie Channel from 1986 to 1996, his TNT series "MonsterVision" ran from 1996 to 2000 and "The Last Drive-in with Joe Bob Briggs" debuted on Shudder in 2018 and is wrapping up this year.

articles.content:
Depop is bringing the fashion of Panem to the resale market.

Ahead of the Nov. 20 theatrical release of " The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ," the secondhand fashion marketplace has teamed up with Lionsgate and the film's costume designer, Bina Daigeler, on a series of shoppable edits inspired by four of the prequel's central characters.

Launching Monday, the collaboration features curated selections of vintage and secondhand clothing inspired by Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada), Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak), Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace) and Effie Trinket (Elle Fanning). Rather than producing new merchandise, the partnership draws on existing inventory from independent Depop sellers. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Jack Lowden Plays Coy About James Bond Rumors: ‘It’s All Very Flattering’ but I’m Not ‘Going to Add to the Noise’ Pierce Brosnan Approves of Callum Turner as James Bond: He's 'So Strong' and I'm 'Eager to See' Who Becomes the Next 007

The four edits reflect the film's mix of 1970s fashion, romantic silhouettes and theatrical Capitol style. Haymitch's rebellious, rock-inspired wardrobe looks like worn-in leather jackets, patchwork button-downs, corduroy pants and workwear boots, while Lenore Dove's Western-influenced bohemian look includes flowing maxi dresses, lace and cowboy boots. Maysilee's vintage glamour comes through in 1960s-inspired halter dresses, satin skirts and opera gloves, while Effie's more extravagant aesthetic features floral prints, corsets, statement jewelry and playful headpieces.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson Is the Smart but Safe Choice to Play James Bond
articles.summary: He might not be as tough as Daniel Craig or as suave as Sean Connery, but Pattinson has a mix of qualities that make him a smart choice.
articles.content:
Once Robert Pattinson entered the chat, you probably knew what was going to happen.

When news leaked two weeks ago that The Batman and The Odyssey actor had auditioned to play James Bond , it seemed extremely likely he would land the part.

Because if Pattinson was auditioning, it meant he wanted the role. And if the in-demand Pattinson was actually down to commit to playing Bond across several films, were producers really going to pick Jack Lowden or Callum Turner?

Pattinson benefited from utterly perfect timing. This year, the actor has been on the hottest streak of his career thanks to co-starring in the indie breakout The Drama , followed by his scene-stealing turn in The Odyssey , followed by his creepy turn in A24's successful Primetime , plus the man has Dune: Part Three coming up.

A couple facts about Primetime might have helped the actor land the role: More than 75 percent of the A24 film's opening weekend audience cited Pattinson as their main reason for buying a ticket, and the film had particularly strong Gen Z turnout (69 percent of the opening weekend audience was under 30).

In other words, if you're betting the return of the Bond franchise on an actor, Pattinson's recent run had to be incredibly reassuring to the top brass at Amazon MGM. He has that combination of movie star appeal plus indie film credibility. Pattinson has also previewed playing a spy during his turn in Tenet and has proven he can lead a franchise across his time on Twilight and The Batman . Plus, director Denis Villeneuve worked with Pattinson on the next Dune , so the two already have a relationship.

That familiarity has a bit of a downside, however. Some are knocking the choice because Pattinson is already so well known from other films. The previous Bonds, by and large, were far less established as movie stars. “Pattinson is too popular” is a pretty weak knock, however.

Pattinson also brings something that the franchise desperately needs: A different vibe (“edgy” is a cheap description, but it fits).

Where Pattinson might come up short, for some, is that he's more interesting than he is traditionally handsome or sexy. The angular Pattinson often has a nervous or uncomfortable quality, which makes him highly watchable, but even his romantic roles tend toward quirkiness. When it came to fulfilling that part of the job description, Turner was probably the best fit.

But one thing Bond producers have struggled with in recent years is how to deal with the character's sexuality. How do you modernize a character who has so often been seen as a sexist, womanizing rogue while still preserving the franchise's escapist “men want to be him, women want to bed him” fantasy that's fundamentally a part of 007? Casting Pattinson might relieve some of the pressure to deliver a traditional Bond and suggest new tones and angles to play.

At 40, Pattinson is also notably older than the other actors who were under consideration. We'd been hearing for years that the franchise's producers were looking to refresh the franchise with a young Bond (oddly enough, Lowden, Turner, Josh O'Connor and Nicholas Hoult are all the same age — 36). Pattinson is actually three years older than Daniel Craig when he was cast, so the whole “young Bond” idea went out the window (Henry Cavill fans are seething this morning, as the 43-year-old actor said in March that he would be considered too old for the part).

Age matters as playing Bond is an intensely physical role and is a decade-plus, multi-film commitment. Craig brought a level of intense physicality and brute force the role that any actor would have a tough time matching. For better or worse, an entire generation associates Bond with a guy who is physically intimidating (one wonders if producers are going to want Pattinson to, you know, buff up a bit — and what that would even look like).

One does wonder, too, what the Bond franchise would have been like with the former odds-on favorite to play the character. Lowden would have been a bolder choice. The Slow Horses star is such an everyman, and so not posh, and is particularly good at combining toughness with vulnerability. A more relatable, everyman Bond could have worked.

Still, Pattinson projects vulnerability as well, and checks so many other boxes — a great British actor, a movie star, a box office draw, Gen Z appeal, handsome, a franchise veteran, and a team player (that last one, as we've previously written, is more important than you might think ).

While some of the other Bond candidates might have been more conventional choices, going conventional was a riskier move. You don't want a Bond who feels like he was grown in a lab to play Bond. You want an actor who can take the role somewhere new. When managing a 62-year-old franchise whose demise has been proclaimed countless times, Pattinson's the smartest, safest choice producers could have made — a proven draw who can leave the character shaken and stirred.

articles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Officially Confirms When Its Story Will End
articles.summary: Saheli Khan as Pavi in Avatar: Seven Havens, episode 1, season 1, streaming on Paramount+, 2026. Photo credit: Paramount+ Avatar: Seven Havens might be currently on the way with Season 2 of the animated series next year, but Paramount+ has already confirmed when the story for the new series is going to end. Avatar: Seven Havens made its successful debut with its premiere season this Fall, and quickly confirmed that three more seasons of […]
articles.content:
The showrunners behind Avatar: Seven Havens had previously noted in interviews that the animated series will be ending after its fourth season , and now Paramount+ has indeed confirmed this to be the case as a recent press release for the animated series has revealed “The series will conclude with Book 4, with premiere details to be announced at a later date.” This means four seasons for this new era of the Avatar: The Last Airbender franchise in total to tell its story.

Avatar: Seven Havens has been taking a much different approach with its story and release than seen with The Legend of Korra . “This one was designed more with a clear end, kind of the way we did with Avatar[: The Last Airbender], where we had pitched the whole story out,” franchise co-creator Michael DiMartino stated about the series' plan with GamesRadar+. Rather than extend its story beyond its originally planned single season outing like seen with The Legend of Korra, Avatar: Seven Havens had begun with this endpoint already in mind.

It's also going to be produced at a much quicker rate than fans might have expected as well. Avatar: Seven Havens showrunner Sehaj Sethi confirmed to ComicBook ahead of the debut season's release that they were already in production on Seasons 3 and 4 as of that time. With Season 2 scheduled to release next year and the third season not long after that, it likely means that Avatar: Seven Havens will be ending with Season 4 on Paramount+ sometime in 2028.

It won't be too much longer before we see what's coming next as the release schedule for Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 confirms Episodes 1-3 will be making their worldwide debut with Paramount+ on May 21, 2027, followed by the release of Episodes 4-6 on May 28th, Episodes 7-9 on June 4th, and the final batch of Episodes 10-13 on June 11th. It has also been confirmed that Season 3 will be coming to the streaming service later in 2027, so it won't be that much of a wait between the seasons either.

With Avatar: Seven Havens Season 3 confirming it's going to release in 2027, and a likely 2028 release for Season 4 after, that means fans are going to get quite a lot of this new era of the franchise within the next two years. Coupled with the also in development spinoff prequel series, Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos , likely releasing in this window as well, and fans have quite a lot to look forward to. Do you think four seasons is enough for Avatar: Seven Havens ? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

EXCLUSIVE : Aymara Films , the company behind Alexander Ullom's It Ends , which was acquired by Neon earlier this year, is lining up a slate of television series after scoring financing from a group including the voice of Donald Duck.

The company, which was founded by filmmaker Elle León Nostas in 2024, has landed financing for its small-screen slate from a group of private investors including Tony Anselmo, who has been the voice of Donald Duck since 1985.

The slate includes a raft of book adaptations and animated projects. Heading it up is an adaptation of Adam Sass's YA novel Surrender Your Sons from Nostas and Rodrigo Bellott. "The Morning Show" star Mark Duplass and his wife, Katie Aselton , star in a new video ad for PETA to promote adopting dogs from shelters.

In the spot, the couple introduces viewers to their three rescues, Murphy, Blue and Frances.
